The natural resonance frequency of the Ba(CoTi)xFe12-xO19 material decreases as the substitution level x increases.
Reducing the ferrite powder size to the monodomain level increases the natural resonance frequency but slightly decreases the maximum microwave energy absorption.
Orienting the ferrite powder in a magnetic field can significantly affect the microwave absorbance characteristics.
The initial Ku-band RAM with just ferrites and epoxy binder can achieve over 12 dB of absorbance across the 12-18 GHz band.
Further optimization of the coating composition and structure could yield over 10 dB absorbance in the 8-18 GHz range.
The Ku-band RAM developed is thicker but lighter in weight compared to conventional ferrite-based RAMs, which is critical for aircraft applications.
The authors used a coprecipitation technique to synthesize the hexagonal ferrite powders.
The hexagonal ferrite powders have an average particle size less than 10 μm.
X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed the ferrite material is a single M-phase.
The saturated magnetization of the ferrite material is 54.0 emu/g.
The relative complex magnetic permeability and dielectric permittivity of the ferrite material were measured across the Ku-band.
Combining the ferrite RAM with other absorbing materials can improve the absorbance to over 20 dB in parts of the Ku-band.
The coated specimens weigh approximately 3.52 kg/m2.
The authors state the successful development of the Ku-band hexagonal ferrite RAM is of significant importance for wide-band stealth material preparation.
The authors used an HP8510B network analyzer to measure the electromagnetic parameters of the ferrite material.
